facts: Preform temperature is set per preform type; the oven profile is part of the recipe, not a free setting.

glossary.definition: The injection-moulded tube that is heated and blown into a bottle.

The rod that stretches the heated preform lengthwise before blowing.

procedures.title: Format changeover
steps: Empty the oven and stop the preform infeed.
Isolate compressed air and verify the carousel is depressurised.
Swap moulds and stretch rods for the new format.
Load the recipe for the new preform and run the oven to temperature.
Blow and inspect the first bottles before releasing the line.

learned.content: Whitish bottle bases usually mean the preform is too cold at the gate — raise the bottom lamp zone first.
learned.context: Recurring on 0.5 L formats after a preform supplier change.

learned.content: A slow pressure drop across all stations points to the high-pressure valve block, not a single mould.

procedures.title: Die change
steps: Stop the press and isolate the hydraulic circuit.
Swap the die for the new format.
Set pressing force and run test tiles.

learned.content: Density differences across a tile usually mean uneven powder loading, not a press fault.
Hydraulic oil above 55 °C comes before most seal failures on this press.
